engine: peaceai/lib/derive-wire-v2.ts (deriveWireLoopDetail, deriveLoop) derives a NEW module from the issue's header signature, Behavior paragraph and data-described fakes / expects, in one closed template (loopModule in peaceai/lib/learned-edit-existing.ts): `import type { T } from "SPEC";` and one `export async function F(LIST: string[], C: { M(ITEM: string, ..): Promise<T> })` that declares the report list R and an empty error list E, goes over LIST in order with `const X = await C.M(ITEM, ..)`, pushes X to R and breaks on STOP (after or before the push), then returns `{ R, E }`. It is reached through the EXISTING_EDIT kind in peaceai/lib/learned.ts when the spec carries the loop vocabulary (statements derived-loop-over-list-new-module-v1, all or none; isWireLoopParams); the candidate creates its module (create: true, allowed in generate.ts for this spec only). The derived module passes the Job B static check (gradeLoopModuleProblem: loopModuleShape re-reads the holes off the graded file and rebuilds it with loopModule byte for byte, loopTypeProblem re-checks the stop fields on T, the hermetic walk runs on the module and on its type-default stub); Job B's before-run source is that stub (loopStub), which must fail by assertions only, then the module is removed.
scope: One new src/ module that does not exist yet (editablePath; the target's denyPatterns apply). The header: `add a new module src/x.ts exporting async F(LIST: string[], C: { M(ITEM: string[, K: "LIT"]..): Promise<T> }) that returns the R and an E list of { f: string; .. }` (1-3 string fields). Each literal argument is the one value of its string-literal type and must be a word of the Behavior paragraph. T: the one exported interface / type alias of that name in the in-scope source, imported type-only in the repo's import style. STOP: the Behavior's one `stops right after a report whose C[ or whose C]` sentence, C = `FIELD WORDS is WORD` (FIELD a non-optional string field of T, or a string-literal union holding WORD) or `FIELD WORDS mention(s) WORD` (a non-optional string-array field of T, some entry includes WORD); FIELD is the words in camelCase. The placement (stop after or before the push) is fitted to the examples: exactly one fits; a never-stop and a stop-after-the-first program must each miss them. Every example calls F directly with a list literal and one fake of C whose M only resolves, each report carrying every stop field with its JS type; one example must end early by the stop and one must go over its whole list (2+ items), each with its call count.

evidence.note: The spec's evidence block is M98's mining, as public-derive-wire-v2's (same family: one function graded by a new fake-driven test). No upstream evidence specific to a new loop-over-a-list module has been gathered; this is a team-picked skill (GAPS G28) and earns no coverage credit.

limits: One module, one function, one loop over one string-list parameter, one collaborator method call per item, one report list and one error list that stays EMPTY (no catch: a failure propagates, so no error message is read or recorded; the per-item catch is public-derive-wire-v2's record ask on the module afterwards). No helper, no new type (T must exist), at most two stop clauses, a stop clause only from the closed set. A stop clause that no example exercises is taken from the prose and the declared type of T (its field must exist with the right type, and every fake report carries it), not pinned by a stopping example.
